sentences.text: Researchers examined a transgenic mouse model lacking one copy of the Arid1b gene in cells forming specific inhibitory interneurons, measuring how these inhibitory interneurons connected with excitatory neurons in brain slices from baby and teenage mice.

The study found that signals sent to the inhibitory interneurons were weaker than usual, which prevented normal spontaneous brain activity needed for neural circuits to mature and likely hindered the brain's ability to process sensory and spatial information correctly into adolescence.

The authors conclude that the reduced excitation of inhibitory interneurons is a key cause of the neural circuit problems seen in these mice, noting that their findings apply only to this animal model.
